title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 1: works path to glory, not cause of decree — Scotus & Bellarmine
pass_a_gloss: From these words nothing else can be gathered than that the sons of God, freely predestinated from eternity unto glory, at length approach that, or are let into it, others being shut out, because these alone by the right way ordained by God have proceeded thither. But what Vasquez presses — that the aforesaid works are named in this place as causes of the preparation itself, or of the eternal Divine destination — is most false. For the true cause is hinted when they are called blessed of the Father. Therefore indeed he destined them to the heavenly inheritance because from his grace he willed to be made their Father in Christ. But their works, neither as foresight nor as done in time, were the cause of predestination unto glory, but of introduction: nor of this are they meritorious causes, but causes only subordinate, in the same sense in which motion on the way is called a cause of arriving at the way's end. In this therefore Vasquez has slipped, that he has not noticed that the act of decreeing or predestinating unto glory can be merely gratuitous in God, and rest on no foresight of human acts: while yet the manner of arriving at glory as to man is laborious, and requires many acts, without which God has ordained and foresaw that he would never put in to the kingdom of glory. Scotus indicated this solution, Lib. 1. dist. 41, where he writes that this proposition, GOD WILLS TO GIVE PETER ETERNAL GLORY ON ACCOUNT OF MERITS, is false, if those words, ON ACCOUNT OF MERITS, be construed with the verb, WILLS: for God did not from foresight of merits conceive the will of glorifying Peter. It is true, if they be construed with the verb, TO GIVE: for he does not will to introduce into possession of glory except after it has been foresight that he walked in those good works which God prescribed and preordained for him. Bellarmine uses the same reply, book 2, On grace and free choice, chapter 13. This proposition, GOD FROM ETERNITY PREDESTINED TO GIVE MEN THE KINGDOM THROUGH FORESIGHT GOOD WORKS, can be both true and false. For if that, THROUGH FORESIGHT WORKS, be referred to the verb, PREDESTINED, it will be false: for it will signify that God predestined men because he had foresight their good works; If it be referred to the verb, TO GIVE, it will be true: because it will signify glorification in execution to be the effect of justification and sanctification or of good works. But this argument will be pressed again, and somewhat more strongly; where we also will answer more fully. Key lemmas: causa introductionis (non praedestinationis); Scotus dist. 41; Bellarminus De grat. 2.13; PROPTER MERITA with VULT vs DARE.
pass_b_english: From these words you may gather only this: God's children, freely predestined from eternity to glory, at last enter it — others shut out — because they alone took the straight road God ordained. Vasquez's claim that the works named here are causes of the preparation itself, or of God's eternal destination, is utterly false. The true cause is hinted when they are called the Father's blessed: he destined them to the heavenly inheritance because by grace he willed to be their Father in Christ. Their works, neither as foresight nor as done in time, caused predestination to glory — only introduction into it; and even of that they are not meritorious causes, only subordinate ones, as motion on a road is a "cause" of reaching the end. Vasquez's slip: he missed that decreeing or predestining to glory can be purely gratuitous in God and rest on no foresight of human acts, while the way of arriving at glory for man is laborious and needs many acts without which God ordained and foresaw he would never put in to glory's kingdom. Scotus (I dist. 41) marks the solution: "God wills to give Peter eternal glory on account of merits" is false if "on account of merits" construes with "wills" — God did not form the will to glorify Peter from foresight of merits — and true if it construes with "to give": he will not bring into possession of glory until it is foresight that Peter walked in the good works God prescribed and preordained. Bellarmine uses the same reply (De grat. et lib. arb. 2.13): "God from eternity predestined to give men the kingdom through foresight good works" is false if "through foresight works" hangs on "predestined," true if it hangs on "to give" — glorification in execution as the effect of justification, sanctification, or good works. This argument will be pressed again, harder; we will answer more fully then.
source_text: Ex his verbis nihil aliud colligi potest, quam Dei filios, ab aeterno ad gloriam gratis praedestinatos, tandem illud adire, vel in illud intromitti, exclusis aliis, quia hi soli per rectam & a Deo ordinatam viam eo perrexerunt. Quod autem Vasques urget praedicta opera hoc in loco nominari ut causas ipsius praeparationis, sive aeternae destinationis Divinae, falsissimum est. Nam vera causa innuitur, quando benedicti Patris appellantur. Ideo siquidem haereditati caelesti illos destinavit quia ex gratia sua voluit effici illorum Pater in Christo. Opera autem illorum, neque ut praevisa, neque ut in tempore facta, erant causa praedestinationis ad gloriam, sed introductionis: neque hujus sunt causae meritoriae, sed causae solummodo subordinatae, eodem sensu quo motus in via causa dicitur perveniendi ad terminum viae. In hoc igitur lapsus est Vasques, quod non animadvertit, actum decernendi vel praedestinandi ad gloriam posse esse mere gratuitum in Deo, & nulla niti praevisione actuum humanorum: cum tamen modus perveniendi ad gloriam quoad hominem sit laboriosus, & requirat multos actus, sine quibus Deus ordinavit ac praevidit illum ad gloriae regnum nunquam appulsurum. Scotus hanc solutionem indicavit Lib. 1. dist. 41. ubi scribit, hanc propositionem, DEUS VULT PETRO DARE AETERNAM GLORIAM PROPTER MERITA, esse falsam, si illa verba, PROPTER MERITA, construantur cum verbo, VULT: non enim Deus ex praevisione meritorum concepit voluntatem glorificandi Petrum. Esse veram, si construantur cum verbo, DARE: non enim vult introducere in possessionem gloriae, nisi postquam praevisum est ambulasse in illis bonis operibus, quae Deus illi praescripsit & praeordinavit. Bellarminus eadem responsione utitur lib. 2. De grat. & libero arb. cap. 13. Haec propositio, DEUS AB AETERNO PRAEDESTINAVIT HOMINIBUS DARE REGNUM PER BONA OPERA PRAEVISA, potest & vera esse & falsa. Nam si illud, PER OPERA PRAEVISA, referatur ad verbum, PRAEDESTINAVIT, falsa erit: significabit enim Deum praedestinasse homines, quia opera illorum bona praeviderat; Si referatur ad verbum, DARE, vera erit: quia significabit glorificationem in exsecutione, esse effectum justificationis & sanctificationis sive operum bonorum. Sed hoc argumentum rursus urgebitur, & aliquanto fortius; ubi nos etiam plenius respondebimus.
